Glutamine is the preferred fuel 
for the enterocytes and assists in 
maintaining intestinal membrane
permeability. Th e supplementation
of another nonessential amino 
acid, arginine, is controversial. 
Because negative outcomes were 
documented in patients with sep-
sis, arginine is not recommended 
for use in these individuals.35
Branched-chain amino acids
include isoleucine, leucine, and
valine. Interest in their role during
starvation and metabolic stress is
linked to their particular metabo-
lism within the skeletal muscle.38
For example, leucine is completely 
oxidized for energy within the
muscle and provides more ATP
than glucose. Th e increased metabolism of branched-chain ami-
no acids within the skeletal muscle may spare other substrates
that are required to meet the metabolic demands of stress.4
Other nutrients that should be considered include the antioxi-
dants: vitamin C, vitamin E, selenium, copper, and zinc.1, 4, 35
